 Coram : Rajnish R. Vyas, J.
 Date : February 03, 2026
Judgment :
1. This is an appeal preferred by the claimant challenging the award passed by the Reference Court.
The original claimants / present appellants have preferred enhancement of compensation.

The
learned

counsel for the appellants has submitted that, while deciding Land Acquisition Reference No.479 of 2010, the Reference Court has not treated Survey No.51/B, owned by him, as a seasonally irrigated land, but treated it as dry land.
He submitted that, while arriving at the said conclusion, the evidence on record was not taken into consideration.
2. Mr. Kakade, learned counsel appearing for the appellants, has relied upon Exhibit 16, which is a 7/12 extract.
According to him, if Exhibit 16, is perused, it would reveal that a pipeline is laid from the river Dudhana, and therefore, it logically follows that the land was seasonally irrigated land.

3. Per contra, Mr. Chawre, learned counsel appearing for the acquiring body, has submitted that the appellants have not made out any case for enhancement of compensation, as there is absolutely no evidence on record.
He further submitted that, in order to claim 936.FA.3608.2019 parity, the claimants will have to show that their lands were also similarly situated.

He has submitted that the entire land admeasuring 2.86 Are cannot be treated as semi irrigated land, since neither any material was produced on record that an electricity meter was installed in the village, nor any witness was examined.

He submitted that a perusal of Exhibit 16 would reveal that, more particularly having regard to the manner in which the crop pattern is mentioned, only part of the land can be treated as seasonal irrigated land.

He contended that the SLAO rightly treated 0.67 Are land as semi irrigated land and 2.19 Are as dry land.
4.

This Court, while deciding First Appeal No.751 of 2012, in which the award passed by the Reference Court deciding the issue of compensation regarding same village, under the same notification, granted enhanced compensation to the tune of  3,750/- per Are for seasonal irrigated land.
The record shows that only 0.67 Are land is seasonal irrigated land.
Mr. Kakade, learned counsel for the appellants, could not bring anything to my notice to show that the remaining land was seasonal irrigated land.
Even Exhibit 16 cannot come to the rescue of the claimant, since neither the cropping pattern nor the necessary entries show on which particular area the crops were 936.FA.3608.2019 taken.

In that view of the matter, I am of the opinion that only 0.67 Are land can be considered as seasonal irrigated land, and accordingly, the claimants / appellants would be entitled to enhanced compensation to the tune of  3,750/- per Are for 0.67 Are land.
In view of it and considering the judgment dated 23 rd December 2025 passed in First Appeal No.751 of 2022, so also in connected matters, the following order is passed.
